The sources behind the bounds

Bibliography

Scope, notation & provenance

Reading the atlas

This atlas collects constructive distributed approximation algorithms and impossibility results. Its default ordering puts constant and iterated logarithmic round regimes first, followed by explicit degree dependencies and slower bounds.

What “constant” means

n is the number of vertices, Δ the maximum degree, α the arboricity, g the genus, and ε an accuracy parameter. A bound independent of n can depend strongly on these other parameters. Each result records the parameters that must be fixed. A bound such as O(log Δ / ε) is shown separately from a uniform O(1) bound. Likewise, O(f(Δ, ε) + log* n) is only O(log* n) when the other parameters are fixed.

Approximation conventions

For minimization, a factor ρ means cost at most ρ·OPT. For maximization, a factor written as 1 − ε denotes value at least (1 − ε)·OPT. A maximization factor written as 2 or 2 + ε uses the reciprocal convention, OPT / value. The result details specify the applicable convention. Lower-bound entries describe an impossible guarantee; their labels are not achievable approximation factors.

Models and implications

LOCAL
Synchronous communication along graph edges, without a message-size restriction. The standard setting gives unique node identifiers.
CONGEST
Typically O(log n) bits per edge per round. Additional restrictions, including broadcast or smaller messages, appear in the assumptions.
Anonymous
No unique identifiers; port-numbering, orientation and any initial coloring must be checked in the individual result.
SUPPORTED
Preprocessing on a support graph is allowed. These bounds are kept separate from ordinary LOCAL algorithms.

The optional model-implication filter includes CONGEST and anonymous upper bounds under LOCAL, and LOCAL lower bounds under CONGEST. It does not convert SUPPORTED results or infer implications between deterministic and randomized settings.

Source checks and coverage

The initial literature map follows Laurent Feuilloley’s Bibliography of distributed approximation beyond bounded degree (v4, November 2023), supplemented by foundational bounded-degree and general-graph results, and selected 2024–2026 work. Every recorded bound links to a source and indicates the location checked. “Primary source checked” means the claim was located in a paper’s abstract or theorem, not that its proof was independently reviewed.

The bibliography also retains supporting exact algorithms, earlier versions, and papers whose bounds have not yet been extracted. Exact symmetry-breaking subroutines are not automatically treated as approximation algorithms. This catalog is not exhaustive: coverage of set cover and packing/covering LPs is selective, and the complete locality lower-bound landscape and some historical or randomized improvements still need expansion. Conference and journal versions can coexist; a paper count is a count of records, not distinct research contributions.

Published claims with subsequently reported proof issues carry a visible source caveat, including inherited dependencies when identified. No automatic “state of the art” label is assigned. Comparing two rows requires compatible objectives, guarantees, graph classes, parameter ranges, randomness, and models. The comparison view preserves those differences.

Data and contributions

The catalog is stored in structured JSON and can be extended with new papers and bounds. Download the full dataset, or export a filtered CSV from the reference view. Select up to four rows to compare their assumptions. Bibliography entries can be exported as BibTeX.

To propose a correction, open a result and choose Download correction template. This prepares a local text file with the exact record and source; it does not submit anything. The project README explains the data fields and validation command.

Acknowledgments

The reference structure is inspired by Florian Schager’s Atlas of Distributed Algorithms. The navy, green, yellow, and pink palette and graph motif draw inspiration from Timothé Picavet’s academic homepage. This is a separate implementation.
